design_direction.rationale: The food is the argument here — ten strong photographs of glossy crepes and the griddle kitchen — so the gallery still leads, but splitting the first screen between the founder's Paris-to-Dallas story and a photograph, set in wide boutique-style type, keeps this from reading like the same photo-behind-a-name page as the last build. Reviews are warm but thin (11 on Yelp, a 3.9 on Google) so stats stay quiet while the photographs and Julien's own story do the selling.
design_direction.signature_why: A type block inset into the corner of the crepe photograph gives the café a Parisian-signage feel rather than the plain photo-behind-name look every other food site uses.

blocks.heading: ALL THE WAY FROM PARIS TO DALLAS —
blocks.text: Dallas is home for Parisian-born and -raised Julien Eelsen who founded Whisk Crêpes Café. His early career with Air France in business management took him to Nigeria, Peru and other parts of the world, but he found the comforts of Dallas synonymous to the comfort and early childhood memories of homemade crêpes with grandma. His love for cooking started at an early age. He remembers sweet memories of picking gooseberries, strawberries and rhubarb with his grandma and aunt to make the jams for the crêpes. While living in Paris, Julien hosted underground dinners for 10 to 50 guests and hosted parties for his friends and family. Julien's work led him to Dallas where he found a fondness for it. A French guy in Dallas, he wanted to open a bistro with French roots but with the Oak Cliff / Dallas culture reflected in it. A laid-back and approachable place for sweet and savory crêpes -- Whisk Crê

testimonials.author: Nani
testimonials.text: I’ve been craving a delicious crepe for months. I was about to order a waffle from Press before I noticed Whisk Crepes Cafe. A staff member recommended the $12 la formule lunch special. I wanted a sweet crepe and decided to make my own. I ordered nutella, bananas, raspberries, strawberries, caramel, and vanilla ice cream. I received powdered sugar but no whipped cream on my crepe. While reviewing photos of the menu I noticed whipped cream should’ve been added. I understand if I declined it, but it’s included in the price. What could’ve been a 5-star review is now 4. Most add-ons are .75. Due to the total amount, I would’ve liked to receive every item. This is the only mishap, and the sweet crepe was the best I’ve ever had! The food-prep area was clean, and the staff were friendly and helpful.

testimonials.author: Schow
testimonials.text: We didn't get crepes but had their nutella latte and hot green tea. I was blown away by the taste! The Nutella latte was out of this world good! I would recommend everyone to try it once! Their drinks were a great compliment on a cold, chilly evening.  Will definitely go back.

testimonials.author: Ram G
testimonials.text: Ok ladies and gents! If you are at Legacy West Food Hall and are craving something sweet you have got to try Whisk Crepes Cafe!!! The Crepes here smack frfr! They have a variety of drinks and deserts and so far everything I have tried is banging!!!! Let’s gooooooooo!!!

testimonials.author: Elan Suret
testimonials.text: The worker served me almond milk when I ordered oat. I asked again is this oat milk and he explicitly answered yes, but  it wasn't oat. I watched him put away almond milk, but I knew that by the taste and the immediate allergic reaction I had as I am ALLERGIC TO NUTS! Smdh. We are living in a horrible era post pandemic. The workers available for these jobs are bottom tier and low vibration. It angers me because I choose to spend 5.00 on 1 ounce of coffee and 1 ounce of milk which is asinine, but I like what I like. It's a treat! Be grateful I'm not vindictive because a mistake like this could cost the company it's life. Please TRAIN your staff!.

testimonials.author: Abdur Rahman Bashir (Imam ARB)
testimonials.text:
Came to Legacy Hall to have waffles from “Press Waffles” when I walked by this place.
I decided to try them out by going to savory route. Oh did I go savory! Tried their G.O.A.T crepe that had dried figs and goat cheese topped with a drizzle of balsamic and pecans with a side of greens.

You have to like goat cheese first in order to appreciate the crepe.  It might not be up your alley but it sure was up mine.

Service was great and the vibe at Legacy Hall was awesome too.
